title: Solidity analyzer throughput, and whether any trial can be qualified

method.statistic: minimum per-file time across trials, with median and worst alongside
why: Contention only ADDS time, so the fastest observed run is the closest available approach to the unloaded figure. The minimum is therefore an UPPER BOUND on unloaded per-file time, not a measurement of it.
The spread between min and worst is contention, and it is reported rather than divided out — a mean over contended trials is a number about the machine, not about the analyzer.
The whole corpus is re-read and re-analysed per trial; nothing is cached between trials, so each is a cold run of the same work the surface artifact measures.

qualification.rule: at least one trial at loadAvg1 < 8
qualification.verdict: UNQUALIFIED — no trial ran below the threshold. The best figure below is an upper bound on the unloaded time, and the repository's own rule for a perf claim is NOT met. The box is shared: a 14-minute poll during this change never saw loadAvg1 below 16, with other agents' processes at ~200% CPU.

limits: A single whole-corpus run per trial, so the figure is a mean over 389 files of very different sizes. The smallest files dominate the per-file average in count terms while the largest dominate in time, and this does not separate them.
Wall time only. No profiling was done, so this says how long and not where the time goes — the TS lane's own perf work is what attributes cost between parse and analyze.
The qualification flag is NOT satisfied by a good-looking minimum. It is satisfied only by a trial that genuinely ran below the threshold, and this run did not.
